sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我对待健康的方式有了很大的不同。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去总是非常专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my Whoop.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我迷上了我的Whoop。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person.
sentences.zh: 说真的，大家知道我是一个非常依赖数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day to day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开Whoop应用程序，看看我的睡眠、压力和劳累程度如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及我每天的感受相关联。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么精英运动员，但我确实从中受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很享受更了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day to day
sentences.zh: Whoop还为我提供了可操作的个性化见解，让我变得更有意识，也意味着我每天能做出更明智的决定，

sentences.en: about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 清楚自己需要什么，而不是一味地踩油门，不停地向前冲。

sentences.zh: 还有人收集香水瓶、咖啡杯、外国纸币，或是80年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是非常私人的事情。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它诉说着我们是谁，也诉说着我们从何而来。

sentences.zh: 在新的播客《Charmed with Sam Todd》中，

sentences.zh: Sam探索了那些成为我们生命一部分的记忆、执念和微小珍宝。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十岁时经历的一些重大人生变化和转折，

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode where we break down this psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新一期节目，我们将继续剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Something that I think a lot of us struggle with, deal with, have on our minds is feeling kind of stagnant in the moment that we're in and in our current life chapter
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都在挣扎、在应对、在思考的一件事，就是感觉在当下的生活阶段中有些停滞不前，

sentences.en: or life season, I guess.
sentences.zh: 或者说是在人生的某个季节里停滞了。

sentences.en: And that is something I've personally been thinking about a lot.
sentences.zh: 这也是我个人一直在思考的问题。

sentences.en: The further I get into my 20s, the more I'm kind of hungering for a life change.
sentences.zh: 随着我步入二十岁的深处，我越来越渴望人生的改变。

sentences.en: And I thought, why not bring on one of my favorite podcasts, one of my favorite people, actually, who has helped me and given me advice,
sentences.zh: 我想，为什么不请来我最喜欢的播客主之一，实际上也是我最喜欢的人之一，她曾通过她的节目《爱、幸福与成功》为我提供过建议，

sentences.en: even if she doesn't know it, through her show Love Happiness and Success to share some of her wisdom with us.
sentences.zh: 尽管她自己可能都不知道，请她来与我们分享她的智慧。

sentences.en: So welcome, Dr. Lisa Marie Bubby.
sentences.zh: 所以，欢迎Lisa Marie Bobby博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 感谢您来到节目。

sentences.en: You are too kind.
sentences.zh: 你太客气了。

sentences.en: And I'm flattered and honored that you listen to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 能听到你收听我的播客，我感到受宠若惊，也深感荣幸。

sentences.en: And it's so wonderful to know that it's been helpful for you.
sentences.zh: 得知它对你有帮助，真是太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太美好了。

sentences.en: That's why I make them.
sentences.zh: 这就是我制作节目的初衷。

sentences.en: So mission accomplished.
sentences.zh: 所以，任务圆满完成。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这太有趣了。

sentences.en: I was saying this to you before.
sentences.zh: 我之前就跟你说过。

sentences.en: Before, people always ask me, like, what do you listen to?
sentences.zh: 以前人们总是问我，你平时听什么？

sentences.en: And I'm like, I listen to this show.
sentences.zh: 我就说，我听这个节目。

sentences.en: I listen to your show.
sentences.zh: 我听你的节目。

sentences.en: I feel like it's so interesting because I'm sure a lot of people listen to this as their source of wisdom and their source of advice.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很有意思，因为我相信很多人把这当作智慧和建议的来源。

sentences.en: But I think also, like, the advice giver also needs, you know, the advice of others and also needs, like, the knowledge of others as well.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，建议的提供者也需要他人的建议，也需要他人的知识。

sentences.en: So thank you so much for the work you do.
sentences.zh: 所以非常感谢你所做的工作。

sentences.en: Do you want to explain a little bit more about who you are, your approach, your maybe journey to where you are now?
sentences.zh: 你想多介绍一下你自己、你的方法，以及你走到今天这一步的历程吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, happy to.
sentences.zh: 没问题，我很乐意。

sentences.en: So, yeah, Lisa Marie Bobby.
sentences.zh: 好的，我是Lisa Marie Bobby。

sentences.en: Gosh, my journey starting in my 20s, trying to figure out what the heck I was going to do in the world.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我二十岁时的旅程，一直在试图弄清楚我到底要在世界上做什么。

sentences.en: And I went through a period in my 20s where I felt very lost and unclear as well.
sentences.zh: 我在二十多岁时也经历过一段感到非常迷茫和困惑的时期。

sentences.en: And actually, we could talk more about this.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们可以多聊聊这个。

sentences.en: So my pivotal moment in my 20s was 9-11.
sentences.zh: 我二十岁时的转折点是9·11事件。

sentences.en: So the terrible, you know, terrorist attacks.
sentences.zh: 那场可怕的恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: My cousin actually was killed in...
sentences.zh: 我的表亲实际上就在那场袭击中丧生了……

sentences.en: He worked at one of the World Trade Center buildings.
sentences.zh: 他在世贸中心的一栋大楼里工作。

sentences.en: It was awful.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了。

sentences.en: But it was this crisis where I was like, what am I doing with my life?
sentences.zh: 但那是一场危机，让我开始思考：我的人生到底在做什么？

sentences.en: And it really led me to do a lot of personal soul searching.
sentences.zh: 这确实促使我进行了大量的自我反思。

sentences.en: And it was right after that that I decided to go back to school to become a therapist, which I began in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 就在那之后，我决定重返校园成为一名治疗师，那是我二十多岁时开始的。

sentences.en: I since became a marriage and family therapist, then did a doctoral degree, became a licensed psychologist,
sentences.zh: 后来我成为了婚姻与家庭治疗师，接着攻读了博士学位，成为了一名持证心理学家，

sentences.en: pursued coaching as a career path, which has been really exciting for me.
sentences.zh: 并将教练作为职业道路，这对我来说非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And so I founded a private practice.
sentences.zh: 于是我创办了一家私人诊所。

sentences.en: It's called Growing Self-Counseling and Coaching.
sentences.zh: 它叫“Growing Self Counseling and Coaching”。

sentences.en: And we have, you know, 50-plus therapists running around here these days.
sentences.zh: 如今我们有50多名治疗师在这里工作。

sentences.en: And also started the Love, Happiness, and Success podcast kind of as a hobby because I love, you know, talking about personal growth and self-development.
sentences.zh: 我还创办了《爱、幸福与成功》播客，算是作为一种爱好，因为我喜欢谈论个人成长和自我发展。

sentences.en: And one of the values that I connected with when I was in my 20s related, you know, with everything that I went through, realized how important it was for me personally
sentences.zh: 我在二十多岁时所建立的价值观之一，与我所经历的一切有关，我意识到对我个人而言，

sentences.en: to be of service to other people.
sentences.zh: 能够为他人服务是多么重要。

sentences.en: And so that's why I started doing my podcast, just to like share things and advice and knowledge and put it out into the world.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我开始做播客的原因，只是为了分享一些东西、建议和知识，并把它们传递给世界。

sentences.en: And that, I mean, so when you were talking about the fact that you enjoy the show and that you've benefited from it, like that's why I do this.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你谈到你喜欢这个节目并从中受益时，这就是我做这件事的原因。

sentences.en: And I can't tell you how happy that just made me here.
sentences.zh: 我无法形容听到这些让我有多开心。

sentences.en: Oh my goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Well, I'm so glad that I could,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我能……

sentences.en: I don't know, I don't know if it's encouragement, but just to share the love, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这算不算鼓励，但我想这只是分享爱吧。

sentences.en: It's so nice when people say that to me.
sentences.zh: 当人们对我这么说时，感觉真好。

sentences.en: So I'm sure that, yeah, it's good to pass that on to everybody who you also benefit from.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信，把这份爱传递给那些也让你受益的人，也是一件好事。

sentences.en: I want to go back to that kind of pivotal moment because I feel like that is firstly so tragic.
sentences.zh: 我想回到那个转折点，因为我觉得首先这太悲剧了。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry that that happened, but I think it's also something that a lot of people in their 20s might relate to, having some major life change, some maybe not a tragedy,
sentences.zh: 我很遗憾发生了那样的事，但我认为这也是许多二十多岁的人可能会产生共鸣的事情，经历某种重大的人生变故，也许不是悲剧，

sentences.en: but a major life event that kind of puts them onto a completely different path.
sentences.zh: 但却是一个重大的人生事件，将他们带上了一条完全不同的道路。

sentences.en: And in other senses, it can also be so gradual, right?
sentences.zh: 而在其他意义上，它也可能是非常渐进的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like this gradual loss of self, this gradual loss of belonging, this gradual sense of like, I just feel really stuck in my life.
sentences.zh: 比如这种逐渐的自我丧失、逐渐的归属感缺失，这种逐渐感觉到“我真的被困在生活中了”。

sentences.en: So why do you think that, why do you think we get to those points where we realize that we need to change?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为，为什么我们会走到那些意识到需要改变的地步呢？

sentences.en: Is it just because of those things, those kind of existential moments that make us question our purpose?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为那些事情，那些让我们质疑人生目标的生存时刻吗？

sentences.en: Or is there something deeper or something more gradual that happens there?
sentences.zh: 还是说那里发生了更深层或更渐进的事情？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I'll tell you a secret, actually, that I don't think is talked about enough in our culture is that the reason we all grow is not despite the challenges
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实我要告诉你一个秘密，我觉得在我们的文化中讨论得还不够多，那就是我们之所以成长，并不是尽管经历了挑战

sentences.en: and the hard times that we go through.
sentences.zh: 和艰难时刻，

sentences.en: It's really because of them.
sentences.zh: 而是正是因为它们。

sentences.en: I'm a big believer in that we really kind of need to make contact with our dark emotions.
sentences.zh: 我坚信我们确实需要与我们的负面情绪进行接触。

sentences.en: And because that's like where a lot of our inner wisdom really is.
sentences.zh: 因为那往往是我们内在智慧所在的地方。

sentences.en: And it's only when you go through something challenging, if it's a crisis, like a building blowing up in a terrorist attack, that would be one example.
sentences.zh: 只有当你经历了一些具有挑战性的事情时，比如危机，像恐怖袭击中大楼爆炸那样，那是一个例子。

sentences.en: But also, it really is a crisis when you get to this place in your life and you're like, I don't know who I am or what I want or what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 但当你走到人生的这个阶段，心想“我不知道我是谁，我想要什么，或者我在做什么”时，这确实也是一场危机。

sentences.en: Like, to really like recognize that and sit with those feelings, it brings up a lot of pain.
sentences.zh: 去真正认识到这一点并与这些感受共处，会带来很多痛苦。

sentences.en: And that too can be its own kind of crisis that can catalyze a lot of really important growth work and personal development.
sentences.zh: 而那本身也可以成为一种危机，能够催化许多非常重要的成长工作和个人发展。

sentences.en: I think people that are just kind of happy to be here and bopping along and feeling good, they don't get to do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为那些只是满足于现状、随波逐流、感觉良好的人，他们没有机会去做这些。

sentences.en: They don't have a reason to do that.
sentences.zh: 他们没有理由去做这些。

sentences.en: And so I think the shift comes in really like appreciating the hard times for what they are, which are these fantastic opportunities that often go unrecognized.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为转变的关键在于真正去欣赏艰难时刻的本质，它们往往是那些未被察觉的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: You know, we try to make it go away rather than understanding them for the gifts they are.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们试图让它们消失，而不是把它们理解为它们所带来的礼物。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这有道理吗？

sentences.en: It makes so much sense.
sentences.zh: 非常有道理。

sentences.en: It reminds me of this quote my mom always says to me, which is, you can either choose to be comfortable or you can choose to grow.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起我妈妈常对我说的名言：你要么选择舒适，要么选择成长。

sentences.en: And so it's in those moments of, yeah, in those moments of the greatest discomfort that we find ourselves changing the most for the better.
sentences.zh: 所以正是在那些最不舒适的时刻，我们发现自己为了变得更好而发生了最大的改变。

sentences.en: But I still think that it's really difficult when you get to that point and you're like, it's interesting what you said.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然认为，当你走到那一步时，你会觉得很难，你说得很有趣。

sentences.en: You're happy to just kind of go with the flow and happy to go along with the status quo.
sentences.zh: 你满足于随波逐流，满足于维持现状。

sentences.en: I'm sure that the people listening to this are perhaps not those people and are perhaps facing a lot of confusion.
sentences.zh: 我相信收听这个节目的听众可能不是那样的人，或许正面临着很多困惑。

sentences.en: How do you navigate that?
sentences.zh: 你如何应对这种情况？

sentences.en: How do you navigate feeling simultaneously quite stuck and also wanting more for yourself?
sentences.zh: 你如何应对那种既感到相当困顿，又想为自己争取更多的心态？

sentences.en: Like what are some of the steps to move into that next chapter of your life when you realize that perhaps you are unhappy?
sentences.zh: 当你意识到自己可能不快乐时，迈向人生下一个篇章的步骤有哪些？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And it's a multi-layered answer because I want to be honest with you and your listeners.
sentences.zh: 这是一个多层面的答案，因为我想对你和你的听众诚实。

sentences.en: And so to not give some trite like thing that, I mean, the truth really is that first of all, it requires a period of exploration in order to understand
sentences.zh: 为了不给出一些陈词滥调，真相其实是，首先，它需要一段探索期，以便理解

sentences.en: what is at the core of the happiness and dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 快乐和不满的核心是什么。
